root_cause.text: `mtk_jpeg_release()` in the MediaTek JPEG V4L2 driver freed the per-file `mtk_jpeg_ctx` without first synchronously cancelling `ctx->jpeg_work`, allowing the queued worker to run afterward and dereference freed context memory.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description and patch both state that `close()` calls `mtk_jpeg_release()`, which previously did `kfree(ctx)`-equivalent cleanup while `queue_work()`-scheduled JPEG encode/decode work from `mtk_jpeg_device_run()` could still be pending or running; the fix adds `cancel_work_sync(&ctx->jpeg_work);` before `mutex_lock(&jpeg->lock)` specifically to prevent the workqueue callback from accessing freed `ctx`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Cancel pending JPEG work during file release to prevent races with context teardown.
intent_record.what: A call to cancel_work_sync(&ctx->jpeg_work) was inserted at the start of mtk_jpeg_release(), before taking jpeg->lock and releasing the m2m context and control handler.
intent_record.how: When a JPEG file context is being released, any pending or running jpeg_work associated with that context is now synchronously canceled first, preventing the work item from executing after the context has begun teardown and avoiding use-after-free or other teardown races.

grouping_result.intent: Cancel pending JPEG work during file release to prevent races with context teardown.

relevance_review.reason: The group directly addresses the root cause by cancelling pending JPEG work during file release, preventing the worker from running after the per-file context has been freed.

candidates.rationale: This releases the per-file M2M context during file teardown, but in the vulnerable version it happened before any synchronous cancellation of ctx->jpeg_work, allowing the queued worker to run later and access freed context state.
This is part of tearing down the per-file context in release; without first cancelling ctx->jpeg_work, subsequent worker execution could dereference already-freed context resources.

vuln_statements.explanation: This releases the per-file M2M context as part of file teardown, but in the vulnerable version it occurred before any synchronous cancellation of ctx->jpeg_work, so the queued worker could still run afterward and dereference freed context memory.
This is another teardown step for the per-file context; because ctx->jpeg_work was not synchronously cancelled first, the worker could execute after this cleanup and access freed context state.
